size_rationale: Small because it is a one-line fix in the login controller, which the prompt points at by naming POST /v1/auth/login and the missing `tokens` field.
prompt: POST /v1/auth/login returns 200 and the user object, but the response has no `tokens` field, so the client never receives an access or refresh token. Register still returns tokens normally.

root_cause.detail: login sends { user, token: tokens }, so the token pair goes out under `token` instead of `tokens`.

fail_to_pass: tests/integration/auth.test.js > Auth routes > POST /v1/auth/login > should return 200 and login user if email and password match
oracle.cmd: npx jest tests/integration/auth.test.js -t 'should return 200 and login user if email and password match'
